query: For eutectic high-entropy alloys intended for structural applications, what single intervention could simultaneously increase strength and ductility? Formulate one testable hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Phase-selective recrystallization (PSR) can simultaneously increase strength and ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys by eliminating weak boundaries and inducing a microstructure that prevents premature crack nucleation.
generation.material_initial_state: Eutectic high-entropy alloy with a mixture of FCC and B2 phases
generation.intervention: Phase-selective recrystallization (PSR) through cold rolling and annealing
generation.conditions: Room temperature, quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests
generation.structural_mediator: Microstructure with a skeletal, non-recrystallized B2 phase and a recrystallized FCC phase
generation.mechanism: PSR eliminates weak boundaries, allowing both phases to contribute to strain hardening simultaneously through high-density dislocation multiplication and a strain-induced B2 to BCT phase transformation
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased strength and ductility, with a uniform elongation of ~33% and an engineering ultimate tensile strength approaching ~2.2 GPa
generation.boundary: Limited by the complexity of acquiring parameter values for the PSR model and the need for further modifications to the theoretical model
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in the exact mechanism of PSR and its effects on the microstructure and mechanical properties

falsification_experiment.design: Quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests on PSR-treated and untreated eutectic high-entropy alloys
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the PSR-treated alloy does not show a significant increase in strength and ductility compared to the untreated alloy, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Paper card. Question: How can the limited ductility of eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs) be overcome to achieve ultra-ductility while maintaining high strength?. System: Ni30Co30Cr10Fe10Al18W2 (at%) eutectic high-entropy alloy consisting of FCC and B2 phases; industrial A357 casting aluminum alloy. Processing: Two cycles of 30% cold rolling followed by annealing at 1200 °C for 20 mins with water quenching; for A357: two cycles of 15% cold rolling at 540 °C for 40 mins followed by two cycles of 30% cold rolling at 540 °C for 40 mins. Test conditions: Quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests at room temperature with an initial strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1; in situ tensile tests in FE-SEM; loading-unloading-reloading tests for back stress measurement. Findings: The phase-selectively recrystallized (PSR) EHEA achieves a uniform elongation of ∼33% and an engineering ultimate tensile strength approaching ∼2.2 GPa.; The PSR EHEA exhibits a fracture true strain of ∼30%, which is double that of the As-cast (AC) alloy (∼14%) and the fully recrystallized (FR) alloy (∼17%).; The fracture true stress of the PSR EHEA reaches ∼1850 MPa, significantly higher than the AC (∼1390 MPa) and FR (∼1460 MPa)
